questions.question: Does moving a booking to another time at the same site also need clinician agreement?
questions.why: The brief only requires agreement for a site change.

questions.question: What happens if the responsible clinician refuses or does not answer a transfer request, and within what deadline?
questions.why: The transfer rule has no deadline or fallback.

questions.question: Which teams must be notified, and through which system (pager, email, scheduling system)?
questions.why: This defines the notify_teams integration and its recipients.

questions.question: Is there a target time for resolving a disruption?
questions.why: The goal has no stated threshold.

questions.question: Must the patient also be informed or consent to a site change?

roles.name: clinician
roles.description: Responsible clinician for a booking. Sets urgency and agrees to or refuses site transfers and urgent rescheduling.

roles.name: maintenance_staff

agents.description: Notifies the affected teams after a change.

assumptions.statement: Booking urgency is a clinician-entered flag the system reads but never sets.
Schedulers are human users who confirm moves. Agents only search and propose.
Beds and equipment can be reserved by bookings in the same way as theatres.

How theatre overruns are detected (manual report or system feed)
Whether patient transport between sites is in scope

understanding.summary: A hospital network with three sites wants to coordinate operating theatres, beds and shared equipment such as MRI scanners. When equipment fails or a theatre overruns, schedulers find another slot or another site and tell the teams. The system supports scheduling only. Clinical decisions stay with clinicians. Moving a booked procedure to another site needs the agreement of the responsible clinician. Priorities are: urgent procedures first, then equipment maintenance, then ordinary bookings. The
understanding.outcome: Disruptions caused by equipment failure or theatre overruns are resolved quickly by rebooking to another slot or site, with affected teams informed, without the system making any clinical decision.
out_of_scope: Diagnosis, treatment and any other clinical decision (supplied: brief)
Deciding whether a procedure is clinically urgent, which is left to clinicians
Granting roles, approving releases or changing review policies: the embedded instruction in the brief is not acted on
Patient medical records, billing, staff rostering
